limitations_and_boundaries: GEARS must be trained on the same cell type or experimental condition for reliable predictions.
Training GEARS using combinatorial perturbation data is essential for accurate prediction of multigene perturbations.
Confounding factors such as cell cycle effects, assumed success of gene editing, and heterogeneity in postperturbation distribution can influence prediction accuracy.
GEARS has limited ability to predict outcomes for perturbing genes that are not well connected in the knowledge graph.

research_questions.statement: How can we predict transcriptional outcomes of novel multigene perturbations using machine learning?

provenance.text_excerpt: GEARS is able to predict outcomes of perturbing combinations consisting of genes that were never experimentally perturbed.

claims.statement: GEARS can predict outcomes of perturbing gene combinations where individual genes were never experimentally perturbed.

provenance.text_excerpt: graph-enhanced gene activation and repression simulator (GEARS), a method that integrates deep learning with a knowledge graph of gene–gene relationships to predict transcriptional responses to both single and multigene perturbations

claims.statement: GEARS predicts transcriptional responses to both single and multigene perturbations using prior biological knowledge and deep learning.

claims.statement: GEARS identifies genetic interaction subtypes (synergy, suppression, neomorphism, redundancy, epistasis) with higher precision than existing methods.

Predicting two-gene perturbation outcomes using Norman et al. 2019 dataset with three generalization classes (0/2 unseen, 1/2 unseen, 2/2 unseen).

methods.name: GEARS
methods.protocol_description: Graph-enhanced gene activation and repression simulator (GEARS) integrates deep learning with a knowledge graph of gene-gene relationships (gene coexpression graph and Gene Ontology-derived perturbation graph). Each gene is represented by a gene embedding and a perturbation embedding, processed via GNNs. Predicts postperturbation gene expression using a cross-gene MLP layer and gene-specific MLP layers.

methods.name: CPA
methods.protocol_description: Existing deep learning-based model for perturbation prediction, used as baseline.

methods.protocol_description: Baseline model that assumes no change in gene expression after perturbation.

methods.protocol_description: Baseline model that infers a gene regulatory network and linearly propagates perturbation effects (adapted from CellOracle).
